problem.name: Random subset sum at cryptographic density
problem.statement_latex: Given independent random integers $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ modulo a modulus $M$ of roughly $n$ bits and a target $t$, find $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ such that $\sum_i a_ix_i=t\pmod M$. Density and the distribution of solutions are fixed as in the representation-algorithm model. These instances appear in knapsack cryptanalysis and as subproblems in decoding. Complexity is measured in classical RAM time and quantum time with either quantum access to classical memory or quantum-accessible quantum memory, as stated.

Density and the distribution of solutions are fixed as in the representation-algorithm model. These instances appear in knapsack cryptanalysis and as subproblems in decoding. Complexity is measured in classical RAM time and quantum time with either quantum access to classical memory or quantum-accessible quantum memory, as stated.

quantum.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(2^{0.2182n})$ time with classical list heuristics, or $\widetilde O(2^{0.2156n})$ with an additional update heuristic, Bonnetain--Bricout--Schrottenloher--Shen quantum walks.
quantum.details_latex: The first walk has memory exponent $0.2182$; the second has memory exponent $0.2110$. A quantum-search variant uses $\widetilde O(2^{0.2356n})$ time and classically stored lists with quantum random access. The walk variants use quantum-accessible quantum memory. Their representation lists, modular filters and update costs are analyzed for the random density-one distribution in the problem statement.

classical.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(2^{0.283n})$ time and space, Bonnetain--Bricout--Schrottenloher--Shen classical representations.
classical.details_latex: The result uses the standard random-instance list heuristics and representations with coefficients in $\{-1,0,1,2\}$. For positive binary integers of polynomial bit length, the general worst-case subset-sum algorithm gives randomized $O(2^{0.49n})$ word-RAM time; the $0.283$ exponent is the stronger bound in this random regime. A direct Boolean verifier for $n$ modular summands of $b$ bits has $O(n(b+\log n))$ gates. With $b=\Theta(n)$, applying the explicit-circuit counting bound gives an exponent of order $n^2/\sqrt{\log n}$, so the representation bound determines the displayed comparison.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedup through a smaller exponential constant in $n$. Both amplitude amplification and quantum walks contribute to the algorithms.

evidence.description_latex: Partial evidence under the stated random-instance and list assumptions. The $0.2156$ result additionally assumes the quantum-walk update heuristic; the $0.2182$ result uses the classical heuristics.

hardware.description_latex: All fast variants are memory-intensive fault-tolerant workloads. The $0.2356$ algorithm uses exponential classical storage with coherent access; the faster walks use exponential quantum-accessible quantum memory. The memory-access model determines the gate cost of a lookup.
